papers.title: The Player Kernel: Learning Team Strengths Based on Implicit Player Contributions
papers.abstract: In this work, we draw attention to a connection between skill-based models of game outcomes and Gaussian process classification models. The Gaussian process perspective enables a) a principled way of dealing with uncertainty and b) rich models, specified through kernel functions. Using this connection, we tackle the problem of predicting outcomes of football matches between national teams. We develop a player kernel that relates any two football matches through the players lined up on the field. This makes it possible to share knowledge gained from observing matches between clubs (available in large quantities) and matches between national teams (available only in limited quantities). We evaluate our approach on the Euro 2008, 2012 and 2016 final tournaments.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于足球比赛结果预测，与FEA代理建模或植入物设计完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses sports outcome prediction using Gaussian processes and a player kernel, with no FEA, surrogate modeling, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification for engineering design, or any connection to biomedical or implant mechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 利用隐式球员贡献学习球队实力以预测足球比赛结果。
summary_zh.method: 基于高斯过程分类和球员核函数，关联不同比赛。
summary_zh.result: 在欧洲杯2008、2012和2016数据集上验证了方法的有效性。
summary_zh.validation: 在三个欧洲杯赛事的历史数据上评估预测性能。

summary_en.motivation: To predict football match outcomes by learning team strengths from implicit player contributions using a Gaussian process framework.
summary_en.method: Develops a player kernel that relates matches through the players on the field, enabling knowledge transfer between club and national team games.
summary_en.result: The approach achieves competitive predictive accuracy on Euro 2008, 2012, and 2016 tournaments.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on historical match data from three major international football tournaments.

papers.title: Predictive Entropy Search for Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization with Constraints
papers.abstract: This work presents PESMOC, Predictive Entropy Search for Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization with Constraints, an information-based strategy for the simultaneous optimization of multiple expensive-to-evaluate black-box functions under the presence of several constraints. PESMOC can hence be used to solve a wide range of optimization problems. Iteratively, PESMOC chooses an input location on which to evaluate the objective functions and the constraints so as to maximally reduce the entropy of the Pareto set of the corresponding optimization problem. The constraints considered in PESMOC are assumed to have similar properties to those of the objective functions in typical Bayesian optimization problems. That is, they do not have a known expression (which prevents gradient computation), their evaluation is considered to be very expensive, and the resulting observations may be corrupted by noise. These constraints arise in a plethora of expensive black-box optimization problems. We carry out synthetic experiments to illustrate the effectiveness of PESMOC, where we sample both the objectives and the constraints from a Gaussian process prior. The results obtained show that PESMOC is able to provide better recommendations with a smaller number of evaluations than a strategy based on random search.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法可用于多目标约束优化问题，适用于植入物设计中的昂贵仿真采样。
llm.why_not_core: No application to FEA or implant biomechanics; no experimental validation; no patient-specific or clinical context.

summary_zh.motivation: 优化多个昂贵黑箱函数并处理约束
summary_zh.method: 预测熵搜索选择评估点以最大化Pareto集熵减
summary_zh.result: 比随机搜索更快找到更优解
summary_zh.validation: 通过高斯过程先验的合成实验验证

summary_en.motivation: Efficiently optimize multiple expensive black-box functions subject to constraints.
summary_en.method: Use predictive entropy search to select evaluation points that maximize reduction in entropy of the Pareto set.
summary_en.result: Achieves better recommendations with fewer evaluations compared to random search.
summary_en.validation: Validated on synthetic experiments with objectives and constraints sampled from Gaussian process priors.

papers.title: Classifying and sorting cluttered piles of unknown objects with robots: a learning approach
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of sorting a densely cluttered pile of unknown objects using a robot. This yet unsolved problem is relevant in the robotic waste sorting business.   By extending previous active learning approaches to grasping, we show a system that learns the task autonomously. Instead of predicting just whether a grasp succeeds, we predict the classes of the objects that end up being picked and thrown onto the target conveyor. Segmenting and identifying objects from the uncluttered target conveyor, as opposed to the working area, is easier due to the added structure since the thrown objects will be the only ones present.   Instead of trying to segment or otherwise understand the cluttered working area in any way, we simply allow the controller to learn a mapping from an RGBD image in the neighborhood of the grasp to a predicted result---all segmentation etc. in the working area is implicit in the learned function. The grasp selection operates in two stages: The first stage is hardcoded and outputs a distribution of possible grasps that sometimes succeed. The second stage uses a purely learned criterion to choose the grasp to make from the proposal distribution created by the first stage.   In an experiment, the system quickly learned to make good pickups and predict correctly, in advance, which class of object it was going to pick up and was able to sort the objects from a densely cluttered pile by color.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究机器人分拣未知物体，与FEA代理模型和生物医学植入物设计完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses robotic grasping and sorting of cluttered objects, with no FEA simulation, no surrogate modeling, no uncertainty quantification, no contact mechanics, and no biomedical context.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决机器人从杂乱堆中分拣未知物体的问题
summary_zh.method: 使用主动学习从RGBD图像预测抓取结果并分类物体
summary_zh.result: 系统能快速学习并正确预测抓取的物体类别，按颜色分拣
summary_zh.validation: 在真实机器人实验中验证分拣效果

summary_en.motivation: This work aims to solve the problem of sorting unknown objects from a densely cluttered pile using a robot.
summary_en.method: An active learning approach is proposed where the robot learns a mapping from RGBD images in the grasp neighborhood to the predicted class of the object picked, without explicit segmentation of the cluttered area.
summary_en.result: The system quickly learns to make successful pickups and correctly predict the object class, enabling sorting by color from a cluttered pile.
summary_en.validation: The approach is validated through actual robot experiments demonstrating effective sorting of objects by color.
